SURFACE: Plain 2-col tab-delim numeric file, no header, no units. Col1 monotonic 1000→3000, step ~1.668. Col2 noisy 5550-13000ish, "intensity" implied.

CONTENT: Col1 values match Raman shift in cm⁻¹ range for graphene G(~1580)+2D(~2700) bands — row 341-348 shows rise starting ~1567 cm⁻¹, consistent with G peak. Physically checks out as cm⁻¹, not nm (graphene Raman shift spans 1000-3000 cm⁻¹; if these were nm, graphene G/2D wouldn't land there for any common excitation laser). So surface (unitless numbers) undersells real convention (Raman shift, cm⁻¹) — file just omits units, doesn't contradict them.
CONTENT VERDICT: NO MISMATCH

MISREADINGS:
- Col1 read as wavelength (nm) instead of Raman shift (cm⁻¹) — evidence: no G/2D band of graphene exists near 1580/2700 nm for any std excitation source; 1580/2700 cm⁻¹ matches known graphene band positions exactly.
- Col1/col2 swapped (treat intensity as x) — evidence: col1 strictly monotonic increasing, col2 fluctuates with peak shape → col1 must be independent (shift) axis.
- Missing "2D peak" mistaken for absent since sample only shows rows near x=3000 (2D center ~2700 not in shown excerpt) — evidence: full file spans to 3000, 2D band (~2700) is within range, just not in the 10-row sample shown; don't conclude it's missing from actual 1200-row data.
- Offset/baseline (~5550-5620 counts) mistaken as zero baseline — evidence: baseline nonzero across shown ranges (row1, row1195-1200), fit must include nonzero offset param as instructed.
